messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — GPU serving pool 'us-west-gpu-prod' reports 100% node utilization and autoscaler at maxNodes=12. Queue growth ~23 reqs/min, current queue length ~1.2k. Throttles (503) observed from router. Dashboard: https://graf.redwood.internal/d/gpu-pool-usw2
anya: seeing it, thanks. Can someone confirm if autoscaler attempted to scale beyond 12?
kevin: autoscaler logs show attempted scale but aborted: \"reached max node count\". CA config: min=3, max=12. We're hitting the policy ceiling.
sam: quick triage — impact windows? are customer-facing endpoints degraded or only background jobs?
kevin: both. latency on real-time generation API up from 120ms -> 1.2s p95, and several customers reporting timeouts (CS pinged). Background batch jobs are throttled into queue.
anya: OK, priority = P1. Steps: (1) try a manual cap bump to 20 nodes (2) if cloud quota blocks, fallback to draining non-critical pools and route traffic to other regions. Who can do manual bump now?
kevin: I can try manual bump. Note: we've had quota alerts in the past for GPU quota in us-west-2; if quota exhausted the API will fail to create instances.
kevin: running command to patch cluster-autoscaler configmap -> set maxNodes: 20
kevin: ```
# kubectl -n kube-system get configmap cluster-autoscaler -o yaml > ca.yaml
# edit ca.yaml set --nodes=3:20:gpu-nodes-usw2
# kubectl apply -f ca.yaml
```
deploy-bot: [deploy] cluster-autoscaler configmap update triggered by kevin. CI/CD job id: 29812.
sam: while nodes are provisioning, watch pending pods. If pods stuck in Pending with "Insufficient resources" we likely need cloud quota or different instance type. Run `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending`
kevin: got a few Pending due to node taints + pod tolerations missing. Some inference pods set tolerateOnlyGPU=true by mistake in the last rollout. Rolling patch to add tolerations.
kevin: ```
# kubectl patch deployment infer-worker -n inference -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'
```
jordan: I'm on cloud support rotation. If cloud quota is the blocker I can open a quota increase request — but that takes ~30-90 mins. Consider moving low-priority inference traffic to preemptible pool or other region as temporary mitigation.
kevin: cluster-autoscaler update accepted by k8s, cloud API called to create 8 more instances. Cloud returned error: \"RESOURCE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED: GPUs per region quota exceeded\". Manual cap bump aborted.
anya: ack. Jordan, please open quota request and mark it urgent 'production-sla'. Sam/kevin — implement fallback routing and reduce concurrency on warm pool to free up slots.
sam: initiating routing change: update traffic policy to reduce capacity used by non-enterprise tenants by 50%. Patching service weights now.
sam: ```
# curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.internal/route-manager/v1/ratelimit -d '{"scope":"non-enterprise","percent":50}'
```
infra-bot: Route adjustment applied. Non-enterprise traffic reduced by 50%. Estimated immediate queue relief: ~300 reqs.
kevin: also found GPUs stuck in Terminating state due to kubelet imagepulldeadline group; manually cleaning orphaned instances to free quota. Running `gcloud compute instances delete <orphan>` now.
kevin: cloud console shows 3 orphaned GPUs; deleting -> should free 3 quota units.
jordan: quota request submitted to GCP support ticket #INC-10456, marked high-priority. ETA 45 mins. Also requested temporary soft quota raise while we stabilize.
customer-success: flagged top 5 affected customers and opened incident notifications with templated message. We're offering retry/backoff guidance and letting them know we're working on it.
kevin: deleted orphan instances. Re-attempting autoscaler scale. Cloud API call succeeded this time — provisioning 5 nodes.
kevin: nodes coming up, kubelet registering them. `kubectl get nodes` shows +5 GPU nodes in NotReady -> Ready loop.
sam: good — pods scheduling. Watching queue drain. Current queue length: 820 -> 420 in 6 min. Error rate dropping.
anya: any blockers left?
kevin: one internal job (batch-warmers) spawned many init-containers and briefly consumed GPU allocation; I scaled that job down from 50 -> 10 replicas to reduce churn.
kevin: batch-warmers scaled down. Cluster stabilized. Queue at ~120 and falling. P95 latency back to ~210ms. Throttles down to near-zero.
jordan: cloud confirmed temporary quota bump will be in place for 2 hours; we can follow up for a permanent increase.
anya: excellent. Runbook items: (A) Post-incident: review autoscaler maxNodes rationale (B) add circuit-breaker to block big warmers during peak (C) add alert for orphaned GPU instances > 10m.
kevin: I'm going to handoff to night on-call. Handoff note: maxNodes now 20 (temporary), quota bump active until +2h, queue draining, core customers notified. If nodes fail to provision again -> immediate page infra-oncall and escalate to cloud support.
sam: taking handoff. I'm on until 0400 UTC. Will monitor queue and node provisioning.
customer-success: will follow up with impacted customers and send postmortem summary when available.
anya: thanks everyone — creating a JIRA for postmortem and action items. Tagging infra and eng-runtime for follow-up. Incident status: mitigated. Root cause: autoscaler policy set too low for peak traffic & cloud GPU quota tightness combined with orphaned instances.
kevin: resolution: manual cleanup + temporary autoscaler cap bump + routing degradation for non-enterprise traffic. Queue drained and services recovered.
sam: closing thread for now. If anything regresses reopen. :white_check_mark:
